conclusion: Independent organic bottom contacts are partitioned by visible model surface, retain collision-safe native root continuations and hand off to actual printed contact planes. Following body/interface paths are height-modulated above stepped contacts while ordered hollow-wall collections retain their order. The source-bound Release passes 31 organic/tree-bridge cases with 3626 assertions and four clearance/interface cases with 119 assertions. Two test2 exports have identical command sequences; the central 1.63-2.40 mm interval has continuous printed support, local bottom gaps are approximately 0.170003 mm, and no significant support/contact volume overlap remains in that interval. Earlier whole-component connectivity and single-floor gap measurements did not certify this local continuity and are superseded. Native roles, widths and patterns are retained; no physical-print or arbitrary-model guarantee is made.
scope: Reviewed source and native Release acceptance on 2026-10-25; historical upstream/performance claims retain their original scope. No hardware print or universal model guarantee.

verification.summary: Relocating a bottom contact without extending its original root leaves a local vertical void. Source-grid collision masks can erase a legal independently sliced root. A footprint crossing model steps requires separate visible surface contacts; succeeding paths require native height modulation over those contacts, including ordered hollow-wall collections.
